_comment: Role GitHub Actions assumes via OIDC. Replace __ACCOUNT_ID__ before use,
then put the role ARN in the repo secret AWS_DEPLOY_ROLE_ARN.
One-time setup -- the OIDC provider is per account, not per repo:
aws iam create-open-id-connect-provider \
--url https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com \
--client-id-list sts.amazonaws.com \
--thumbprint-list 6938fd4d98bab03faadb97b34396831e3780aea1
THE NUMERIC IDS IN THE SUBJECT ARE DELIBERATE. GitHub appends immutable
ids to the owner and repo segments: @39056884 is the account id and
@1412523092 the repository id. The plain name form
repo:chance221/Global_Partners_BA_Data_Pipeline:environment:production
does NOT match and fails with 'Not authorized to perform
sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity'. Matching the ids is also stronger: a
name-based subject can be satisfied by whoever registers the name after a
repo or account is deleted, while the ids cannot be reused.
A repo TRANSFER changes the owner id, and these ids are not secret --
GitHub exposes both through its public API.
To re-derive them, print the claims from a workflow run:
TOKEN=$(curl -sH "Authorization: bearer $ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN" \
"$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=sts.amazonaws.com" | jq -r .value)
echo "$TOKEN" | cut -d. -f2 | base64 -d | jq .sub
Only ever decode the payload -- the whole token is a credential.
HOW THE MAIN-ONLY GATE WORKS -- the division of labour matters:
GitHub enforces the branch. The environment subject carries no ref, so
AWS cannot see which branch a run is on. The restriction lives in
Settings > Environments > production > Deployment branches and tags,
set to the main branch.
AWS enforces the repo and the environment. That is all it can see.
The workflow must declare `environment: production` on the publish job,
or the subject is the ref form and every assume-role is denied.
Two condition operators in one Condition block are ANDed, and a token has
a single sub claim -- so pairing a StringEquals on one subject form with a
StringLike on another can never match. One operator, one subject form.

Statement._comment: Confined to artifacts/. CI has no reason to touch raw, the warehouse, or anything else, and this role is the one most exposed to a supply-chain mistake.

For the update-job step, which is not written yet -- it needs the real JobUpdate shape from the first manually created job. GetJob is here so CI can diff before applying. Deliberately no CreateJob or DeleteJob: jobs are created by hand, CI only updates them.
